One phone per paired HID session
Your phone becomes a real Bluetooth gamepad, keyboard, or mouse. The host sees a standard HID device — no drivers, no server, no account.
Get PocketPad from Google Play. Grant Bluetooth permissions when asked.
Open PocketPad → Connect → select Bluetooth as the transport (not Wi‑Fi).
Tap Prepare for pairing. The app registers the correct HID profile for your current layout (gamepad vs keyboard/mouse).
On your PC: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Add device → Bluetooth. On Mac: System Settings → Bluetooth. Select your phone and confirm pairing on both sides.
Back in PocketPad, open a Gamepad, Universal, Media Remote, or Slide Controller layout. Input is live immediately after pairing.
Wake sleeping PCs before pairing — Bluetooth may stay idle until the host is active.
Switching between gamepad and keyboard/mouse modes usually requires Prepare for pairing again.
Remove stale Bluetooth entries for your phone on both devices if pairing fails.
Some TVs mute speakers when treating the phone as a Bluetooth audio device — disable media audio for the phone in Bluetooth settings if needed.
Connect over Wi‑Fi with PocketPad Companion (Windows)
Install the free PocketPad Companion on Windows for LAN discovery, virtual Xbox controllers (ViGEm), pairing codes for Universal layouts, and multiple phones at once.
Install the EXE installer from the PocketPad overview page. Checksums: README.txt.

Companion is new, so Windows may not recognise it yet. If your browser flags the download, open Downloads (Ctrl + J) and choose Keep (Chrome: Keep anyway). If you see “Windows protected your PC”, click More info → Run anyway. Then approve UAC. The installer adds ViGEmBus when missing (needed for virtual gamepads). Allow PocketPad Companion on private networks in Windows Firewall.
Connect your phone and PC to the same LAN. Avoid guest networks that block device-to-device traffic.
Launch Companion and connect from the phone
Open Companion on Windows. On your phone, open PocketPad → Connect → choose Wi‑Fi → tap your PC when it appears in the list.
For Universal keyboard & mouse layouts, open Companion Settings and enter the 6-digit code shown on the phone when prompted.
Repeat on additional phones — each device shows as Gamepad 1, 2, 3… in Companion for couch co-op.
Prefer Bluetooth on Windows if you only need one phone and want zero install — Companion is optional.
Keep Companion and phones on the same Wi‑Fi band (5 GHz vs 2.4 GHz) for stable discovery.
Phone not listed in Bluetooth on PC
Tap Prepare for pairing first, then scan. Clear old pairings for your phone on both devices.
Check Windows Firewall (private networks), same subnet, and that Companion is running.
Use a gamepad layout; on Windows Wi‑Fi ensure ViGEmBus is installed via Companion setup.
